title: IB Mathematics AA SL
blurb: Topic-focused practice across the five SL syllabus topics — Number & Algebra, Functions, Geometry & Trigonometry, Statistics & Probability and Calculus — at Paper 1/2 short-question difficulty.

units.title: Number & Algebra
units.blurb: Sequences and series, exponents and logarithms, the binomial theorem.

units.title: Functions
units.blurb: Composite and inverse functions, quadratics, rational functions and transformations.

units.title: Geometry & Trigonometry
units.blurb: Radians, the sine and cosine rules, exact values and trigonometric equations.

units.title: Statistics & Probability
units.blurb: Summary statistics, probability laws, conditional probability and the binomial distribution.

units.title: Calculus
units.blurb: Differentiation, tangents, stationary points, and definite integrals with areas.

forms.title: Arithmetic sequences: the nth term
forms.skill: Apply u_n = u_1 + (n-1)d without the off-by-one.

variants.statement: An arithmetic sequence has first term $u_1 = 2$ and common difference $d = 3$. Find $u_{11}$.
variants.explanation: Use $u_n = u_1 + (n-1)d$: $u_{11} = 2 + 10 \cdot (3) = 32$. Multiplying $d$ by $n$ instead of $n-1$ is the classic slip — it gives $35$.

forms.title: Geometric sequences: the nth term
forms.skill: Apply u_n = u_1 r^(n-1), including fractional ratios.

variants.statement: A geometric sequence has first term $u_1 = 2$ and common ratio $r = 2$. Find $u_{5}$.
variants.explanation: Use $u_n = u_1 r^{\,n-1}$: $u_{5} = 2 \cdot \left(2\right)^{4} = 32$. One factor of $r$ too many gives $64$.

forms.title: Arithmetic series
forms.skill: Sum n terms with S_n = n/2 (u_1 + u_n).

variants.statement: An arithmetic sequence has $u_1 = 2$ and common difference $d = 3$. Find the sum of the first 10 terms.
variants.explanation: The last term is $u_{10} = 29$, so $S_{10} = \dfrac{10}{2}(u_1 + u_{10}) = \dfrac{10}{2}(2 + 29) = 155$. Dropping the $\frac{1}{2}$ doubles it to $310$.

forms.title: Laws of logarithms
forms.skill: Add logs of the same base by multiplying arguments.

variants.statement: Find the value of $\log_{2} 2 + \log_{2} 4$.
variants.explanation: $\log_{2} 2 = 1$ and $\log_{2} 4 = 2$, and logs of the same base add: $1 + 2 = 3$. (Equivalently $\log_{2}(2 \cdot 4) = \log_{2} 8 = 3$.) Multiplying the two logs gives $2$ — addition of logs multiplies the ARGUMENTS, not the logs.

forms.title: Infinite geometric series
forms.skill: Test |r| < 1 and apply S = u_1/(1 - r).

variants.statement: An infinite geometric series has first term $u_1 = 6$ and common ratio $r = \frac{1}{3}$. Find the sum of the series.
variants.explanation: Since $|r| = \frac{1}{3} < 1$ the series converges, and $S_\infty = \dfrac{u_1}{1 - r} = \dfrac{6}{\frac{2}{3}} = 9$. Writing $1 + r$ in the denominator gives $\frac{9}{2}$.

variants.statement: Find the coefficient of $x^{1}$ in the expansion of $(x + 3)^{4}$.
variants.explanation: The general term is $\binom{4}{r} x^{r} \cdot (3)^{4-r}$; for $x^{1}$ take $r = 1$: $\binom{4}{1}(3)^{3} = 4 \cdot 27 = 108$. Putting the power of $3$ on the wrong factor gives $12$.

forms.title: Composite functions
forms.skill: Evaluate (f o g)(a) inner-function-first.

variants.statement: Let $f(x) = 2x + 1$ and $g(x) = x^2 + 2$. Find $(f \circ g)(3)$.
variants.explanation: Inner first: $g(3) = 11$. Then $f(11) = 2 \cdot 11 + 1 = 23$. Composing in the wrong order gives $(g \circ f)(3) = 51$.

variants.statement: The point $(2,\ 3)$ lies on the graph of $y = f(x)$. Find the image of this point on the graph of $y = 2f(x - 1) + 1$.

variants.statement: The point $(2,\ 3)$ lies on the graph of $y = f(x)$. Find the image of this point on the graph of $y = 2f(x + 1) + 1$.
variants.explanation: $x - -1$ shifts the graph $1$ units left, and the output is stretched by $2$ THEN translated by $1$: the image is $(2 - 1,\ 2 \cdot 3 + 1) = (1,\ 7)$. Adding $1$ before multiplying gives $(1,\ 8)$.

forms.title: The discriminant
forms.skill: The sign of b^2 - 4ac counts the real roots without finding them.

variants.statement: How many real roots does $x^2 - 9x - 6 = 0$ have?
variants.explanation: The discriminant is $b^2 - 4ac = (-9)^2 - 4(1)(-6) = 105$, which is positive — so the equation has two distinct real roots. Its SIGN is the whole answer; the roots themselves never have to be found.

forms.title: Arc length in radians
forms.skill: Use s = r·theta (and know when it is the sector area instead).

variants.statement: A circle has radius $3\,$cm. Find the length of the arc subtended by a central angle of $\frac{1}{6}\pi$ radians.
variants.explanation: In radians, arc length is $s = r\theta = 3 \cdot \frac{1}{6}\pi = \frac{1}{2}\pi$ cm. $\frac{1}{2}r^2\theta = \frac{3}{4}\pi$ is the SECTOR AREA — the other half of this formula pair.

variants.statement: In triangle $ABC$, $b = 3$, $c = 5$ and $\hat{A} = 60^\circ$. Find $a^2$.
variants.explanation: Cosine rule: $a^2 = b^2 + c^2 - 2bc\cos A = 9 + 25 - 2 \cdot 3 \cdot 5 \cdot \left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = 19$. With $\hat{A} = 60^\circ$, $\cos A = \frac{1}{2}$ — the sign of the cosine is where this question is won or lost.

forms.title: Area of a triangle
forms.skill: Apply Area = (1/2) ab sin C.

variants.statement: In triangle $ABC$, $a = 4$, $b = 6$ and $\hat{C} = 30^\circ$. Find the area of the triangle.
variants.explanation: Area $= \frac{1}{2}ab\sin C = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 4 \cdot 6 \cdot \sin 30^\circ = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 24 \cdot \frac{1}{2} = 6$. Since $\sin 30^\circ = \frac{1}{2}$, dropping EITHER the $\frac{1}{2}$ or the sine leaves $12$.

variants.statement: How many solutions does the equation $2\sin x = 1$ have for $0 \le x < 2\pi$?
variants.explanation: $\sin x = \frac{1}{2}$ with $\left|\frac{1}{2}\right| < 1$ crosses the sin curve twice in one full turn. Sketch one period before counting — the graph answers this faster than algebra.

forms.title: Volume of a cone
forms.skill: V = (1/3) pi r^2 h — the third is what separates it from the cylinder.

variants.statement: A cone has radius $4$ cm and height $3$ cm. Find its volume in cm$^3$, giving the answer as a multiple of $\pi$.
variants.explanation: $V = \tfrac13\pi r^2 h = \tfrac13\pi \cdot 16 \cdot 3 = 16\pi$. Dropping the $\tfrac13$ gives the CYLINDER on the same base — exactly three times too big.

forms.title: Probability of a union
forms.skill: Apply P(A u B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A n B).

variants.statement: Events $A$ and $B$ satisfy $P(A) = \frac{3}{10}$, $P(B) = \frac{1}{5}$ and $P(A \cap B) = \frac{1}{10}$. Find $P(A \cup B)$.
variants.explanation: $P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A \cap B) = \dfrac{3}{10} + \dfrac{2}{10} - \dfrac{1}{10} = \frac{2}{5}$. Adding without subtracting counts the overlap twice.

forms.title: Conditional probability
forms.skill: Restrict the sample space before dividing.

variants.statement: In a class, $6$ girls play an instrument and $4$ do not; $5$ boys play and $6$ do not. A student is chosen at random. Given that the student is a girl, find the probability that she plays an instrument.
variants.explanation: Conditioning on "girl" restricts the sample space to the $10$ girls: $P(\text{plays} \mid \text{girl}) = \dfrac{6}{10} = \frac{3}{5}$. $\dfrac{6}{21}$ is the JOINT probability — dividing by the whole class is the standard trap.

variants.statement: A biased coin lands heads with probability $\frac{1}{3}$ on each independent toss. It is tossed $4$ times. Find the probability of exactly $3$ heads.
variants.explanation: $X \sim B(4, \frac{1}{3})$, so $P(X = 3) = \binom{4}{3} \left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{3}\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^{1} = \frac{8}{81}$. Without the $\binom{4}{3} = 4$ factor you count only ONE ordering of the heads.

forms.title: Equation of a tangent
forms.skill: Gradient from f', line through the point of tangency.

variants.statement: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve $y = x^2 + 2x + 1$ at the point where $x = 1$.
variants.explanation: $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2x + 2$, so the gradient at $x = 1$ is $m = 4$, and the point is $(1, 4)$. Then $y - 4 = 4(x - 1)$ gives $y = 4x$. The $y$-intercept is NOT $f(1)$ unless the point of tangency is on the $y$-axis.

forms.title: Kinematics: at rest
forms.skill: Solve v = ds/dt = 0, not s = 0.

variants.statement: A particle moves in a straight line with displacement $s(t) = 6t - t^2$ metres after $t$ seconds. Find the time at which the particle is instantaneously at rest.
variants.explanation: At rest means $v = \dfrac{ds}{dt} = 0$: $v(t) = 6 - 2t$, so $t = \dfrac{6}{2} = 3$ s. Solving $s(t) = 0$ instead gives $t = 6$ — that is when the particle RETURNS, not when it stops.

forms.title: Area under a curve
forms.skill: Integrate between the x-intercepts.

variants.statement: The curve $y = x(2 - x)$ meets the $x$-axis at $x = 0$ and $x = 2$. Find the area of the region enclosed by the curve and the $x$-axis.
variants.explanation: Area $= \displaystyle\int_0^{2} (2x - x^2)\,dx = \left[\frac{2x^2}{2} - \frac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^{2} = \frac{4}{3}$. Both terms matter: dropping either one leaves $\frac{1 b^3}{2}$- or $\frac{1 b^3}{3}$-type values.

forms.title: Stationary points
forms.skill: Solve f'(x) = 0; the constant term can never move one sideways.

variants.statement: Find the $x$-coordinate of the stationary point of $f(x) = x^2 + 16x - 5$.
variants.explanation: A stationary point is where $f'(x) = 0$. Here $f'(x) = 2x + 16$, which vanishes at $x = -8$. The constant $-5$ shifts the curve up or down and can never move a stationary point sideways.
